solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conservative cult around, bizarrely, a bloke never featured in The Mirror

definitions.text: bloke never featured in The Mirror

indicators.note: bizarrely says the letters of these words are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: A political smear: a Tory cult has gathered around some man who is never pictured in the Daily Mirror tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarrely' rearranges CULT AROUND into OUNTDRACUL, which sits between C and A. 'The Mirror' looks like the British tabloid newspaper, but it is a looking-glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires cast no reflection in folklore, so Stoker's famous vampire count never appears in a looking-glass.

clue.text: I've served up stuffing for cold and hot lamb

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: stuffing says the turned letters fill the inside of the word hot

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the letters are written upwards, back to front

parts.note: the letters of I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cook boasts of serving stuffing for lamb dishes both cold and hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the clue's I'VE upwards in this down entry; 'stuffing' looks like a food but puts that inside the word hot, after the cold tap letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheviot is a breed of hill sheep from the Scottish Borders, so a young one is such a breed.

clue.text: Lacking a piece (like Milos's Aphrodite)

definitions.meaning: a piece is slang for a gun, so this means carrying no weapon
the Venus de Milo statue of Aphrodite has lost both arms

explanation.surface: Someone missing a part, like the famous armless statue found on the Greek island of Milos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a fragment of the statue, but it is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a weapon, and also literally without arms, as the statue is.

clue.text: Honk horn, at first long- suffering

parts.note: to toot is to honk a horn

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of horn is used

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A driver who honks the horn, at first, out of long-suffering patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long-suffering' reads as one word, but 'long' gives ACHE and 'suffering' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental pain is a kind of affliction or pain endured.

clue.text: Experts know these guys

definitions.meaning: experienced people are said to know the ...
guys are lines that hold a tent or mast steady

explanation.surface: Specialists are acquainted with these men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' looks like men but means guy lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing the ropes is an idiom for expertise, and guy lines are cords.

clue.text: Sole trader in fruity drink

definitions.meaning: someone who repairs the soles of shoes for a living
an iced drink of wine or sherry, sugar and fruit slices

explanation.surface: A one-person business sells a fruit cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole trader' is a business term for a self-employed person, but here the sole is the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender is the classic tradesman of soles, and the iced cocktail shares the name.

clue.text: Having suddenly changed direction, enticed to take in Switzerland

indicators.note: to take in says the country code goes inside the word for enticed

parts.note: lured means enticed or tempted
CH is the international code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly swerved after being tempted into a trip to Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurch is to make an abrupt, unsteady movement, swaying off course.

clue.text: Lab engineer of histamide prescribed orally by Spooner

definitions.text: Lab engineer of histamide prescribed orally by Spooner

parts.words: Lab engineer of histamide prescribed orally by Spooner
parts.note: histamide, said aloud with its opening sounds swapped Spooner-fashion, becomes Mister Hyde, the brute created in a laboratory by Stevenson's scientist

explanation.surface: A pharmacologist who made a drug called histamide, given by mouth, by a Dr Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spoonerism only turns 'histamide' into Mister Hyde, part of the description; nothing builds the answer's letters, so the whole clue is one cryptic description of his maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's laboratory scientist brewed the drug that released his evil alter ego.

clue.text: Herb, going past Ohio, turned his ass around

indicators.note: going past puts the herb's next letters after the Ohio letter, as if travelling beyond it

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

indicators.note: turned, together with around, says the animal's name is written backwards

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass of Asia, here one belonging to him

explanation.surface: Someone named Herb drives past Ohio and turns his donkey around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' reads as a man's name but is the definition. 'turned ... around' reverses the wild ass's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a fragrant culinary plant of the mint family used in Italian cooking.

clue.text: "Back up, bub" clutching good recipe for chicken in a basket

indicators.note: Back here means the following short word is written in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

indicators.note: clutching means the word bub holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: taken as written: bub is an American form of address to a man
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin recipe, 'take', on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cook tells a pal to back off while holding a decent recipe for a basket meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses UP to PU; BUB then holds G and R, giving BGRUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken in a basket is a classic British bar meal, an example of food served in pubs.

clue.text: Massage upset involved naked seraglio getting bottom pinched; such wicked men!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue says the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to rub is to massage

indicators.note: involved says the letters of naked are twisted together into a new order
getting bottom pinched says the last letter of the word is stolen away

parts.note: a seraglio is a harem, the women's quarters of a palace

explanation.surface: A lurid tabloid tale of an overturned massage in a harem where someone's bottom was pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses RUB to BUR, 'involved' rearranges NAKED into KEAND, and HAREM loses its last letter M. Burke and Hare murdered people in 1820s Edinburgh to sell corpses to anatomists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh pair killed sixteen victims to supply bodies for dissection, so they are notorious villains.

clue.text: One featured in president Hoover's first victory

indicators.note: featured in says the numeral sits within the president's name

parts.note: Trump is a US president
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Hoover's is used

explanation.surface: A news item about a win, the first one appearing under President Hoover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'president Hoover' looks like one person, Herbert Hoover, but the president is TRUMP and Hoover only gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great success or win, a near synonym of a victory.

clue.text: Totally rejected ruthenium, hydrogen + another element

indicators.note: Totally rejected means the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: Ru is the chemical symbol for ruthenium
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
the sign + is read as the word plus

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: ruthenium was thrown out, so hydrogen is combined with a different element instead.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, H and PLUS (the + sign read as a word) are written in that order and the whole run is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur is a chemical element, symbol S, so it is one more element after the two named.

clue.text: Breastfeeds regularly, yet is criticised!

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of Breastfeeds is taken, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A mother nurses her baby at regular times and still gets judged for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is an old sense meaning to scold or berate them angrily.

clue.text: With which Charlie's blowing head off game bird?

definitions.text: With which Charlie's blowing head off game bird?

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the bird's name is removed

parts.note: a partridge is a game bird shot for sport

explanation.surface: A shooting party asks what Charlie used to blast the head off a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus ARTRIDGE (PARTRIDGE without its first letter) builds the answer, while the whole clue describes the shot that loads a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun cartridge holds the powder and pellets that a shooter fires at birds.

clue.text: Engineer on route sees northbound services

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
ST is short for street, a route through town

indicators.note: northbound in a down clue means the word is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: spots means sees or notices

explanation.surface: A road engineer spots service stations heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northbound' reverses SPOTS to STOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorway services are roadside places where drivers pause for fuel and food.

clue.text: I resolved to transform characters like the 25s

indicators.note: to transform says these letters change into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone decides to reform the shady types, like those listed at 25.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25s are outliers: the villains placed around the grid's outer edge, such as the vampire count and the Edinburgh body-snatchers.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter entries are all monsters and murderers, wrongdoers or wicked people.

clue.text: See 19
Evacuate carriage, finding alien in tube

indicators.note: in says the alien goes inside the tube

parts.note: a drain is a pipe or tube
ET is the extraterrestrial from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A railway carriage is cleared because an alien turned up on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' looks like London's Underground, but it is a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a train is to leave its coach, emptying it of passengers.

clue.text: One refusing to accept meat in transit, say?

indicators.note: in says the example abbreviation goes inside the van

parts.note: the Ford Transit is a common British van
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone on the move, perhaps, who won't accept meat offered to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transit' looks like travelling, but a Ford Transit is a British van model.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats no animal products at all, so declines any flesh food.

clue.text: He introduced fifty to grisly primeval death

indicators.note: introduced, with to, says the numeral is put inside the jumbled letters
grisly says the letters of primeval death are horribly mangled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A man who brought fifty people to a gruesome, primitive end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grisly' rearranges PRIMEVAL DEATH and L goes into it. Vlad III of Wallachia, an inspiration for Dracula, executed enemies on stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's pronoun stands for the man himself, a fifteenth-century Romanian prince.

clue.text: For information, Italian turned over an alpine flower

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: turned over says the abbreviation is flipped, read backwards

parts.note: IT is short for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: An Italian looks up a mountain bloom for some facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentians are blue-flowered plants of high mountain meadows such as the Alps.

clue.text: Somewhat revolting, Margaret spayed dog

indicators.note: revolting says the hidden letters are read backwards
Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Margaret's dog was neutered, and someone finds that rather disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgust but here means turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: A yapster is a yapping dog, a noisy little hound.

clue.text: Frost Report seen at 9?

indicators.note: Report says we go by how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A reference to The Frost Report, the old David Frost TV show, being shown at nine.
explanation.walkthrough: At 9-across PUB GRUB has two halves that sound alike. 'The Frost Report' was a 1960s British TV satire show.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words of the phrase at nine end in the same sound, which is an example of matching sounds.

clue.text: Stop silly aunt visiting school

indicators.note: visiting says the jumbled letters go inside the school's abbreviation
silly says the letters of aunt are jumbled

explanation.surface: A command to halt a daft aunt who is calling at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb meaning halt a person, but here it is staunching a flow; 'silly' jumbles the aunt and 'visiting' sets her inside the school abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch is to stem a flow, especially of blood, so it means to halt.

clue.text: The King and I actor invites dance ensemble round for a song

indicators.note: ensemble round says the whole assembled piece is turned around
invites means the actor's first name takes the dance inside it

parts.note: Yul Brynner starred as the King of Siam in The King and I
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A stage star hosts a dance troupe to rehearse a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invites' puts the dance inside the actor's first name; 'ensemble round' then turns the whole combination back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a gentle song sung to send a child to sleep.

clue.text: A peripheral figure to unmask reputedly dishonest character

parts.note: to out someone is to expose or unmask them

indicators.note: reputedly says we go by what is said, the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a liar is a dishonest person

explanation.surface: A plan to expose a figure on the fringes who is said to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reputedly' looks like 'by reputation' but signals the word LIAR is heard as LIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlier is a person or data point lying far from the rest, out on the edges.

clue.text: Honest, intense work by Shelley

definitions.note: short for a work by Shelley, the novel being named

parts.note: frank means honest and open

indicators.note: work says the letters of intense are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A review praising a candid, powerful piece written by Mary Shelley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' does double duty: it rearranges INTENSE into ENSTEIN and also belongs with 'by Shelley' as the novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley wrote the Gothic novel about a scientist who builds a creature.
